title: Psychiatric Disorders: How They Are Classified
source: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine, Psychiatry chapter (groups follow the ICD headings it uses; check against your edition)

beats.vo: Psychiatry has hundreds of diagnoses. But you only need eight groups to start.
Here is the classification, the way Davidson teaches it.

beats.name: Organic
beats.key: A physical illness is driving the mind
beats.vo: One. Organic disorders. Delirium and dementia. A physical illness is driving the mind, so rule it out first.

beats.name: Substance use
beats.vo: Two. Substance use disorders. Alcohol and drugs, from harmful use to dependence.

beats.name: Psychotic
beats.key: Lost touch with reality: delusions, hallucinations
beats.vo: Three. Schizophrenia and other psychoses. The patient loses touch with reality: delusions and hallucinations.

beats.name: Mood
beats.key: A sustained change in mood: lows, or highs and lows
beats.vo: Four. Mood disorders. Depression, and bipolar disorder with its highs and lows.

beats.name: Anxiety & stress
beats.key: Fear and worry out of proportion to the threat
beats.vo: Five. Anxiety and stress-related disorders. Panic, phobias, OCD and PTSD. Fear out of proportion to the threat.

beats.name: Somatic symptom
beats.key: Real physical symptoms, no disease that explains them
beats.vo: Six. Somatic symptom disorders. Real physical symptoms, but no disease that explains them.

beats.name: Eating
beats.key: Disturbed eating driven by weight and shape
beats.vo: Seven. Eating disorders. Anorexia and bulimia nervosa, driven by weight and shape.

beats.name: Personality
beats.vo: Eight. Personality disorders. Enduring patterns of thinking and behaving that start by early adulthood.
Organic. Substance. Psychotic. Mood. Anxiety. Somatic. Eating. Personality.
On the ward, always rule out organic causes first. Save this for your psychiatry posting.
